Functional programming
What functional programming means in JavaScript: pure functions, a pipeline of small functions with pipe, and Maybe from head and fromMaybe in Sanctuary.
Understand what functional programming is: declarative development based on pure functions, in which a task is solved by a pipeline of small functions.
text
Functional programming is high-level, declarative development based on pure functions. Functional programming is a programming paradigm that relies on functions as its primary building blocks.
Pure functions are functions that return the same result for the same arguments and produce no side effects.
code
Functional programming is high-level, declarative development based on pure functions. Functions are its primary building blocks.
Pure functions return the same result for the same arguments and produce no side effects.
In the example, the task is solved by a pipeline of small functions built with pipe: keep the users who are online, then those older than 20, take the first one and get their name.
head returns a Maybe: Just (user), or Nothing if the list is empty. fromMaybe takes the value out of the Maybe and substitutes a fallback for Nothing.
You don't have to build excessive abstractions: they can sometimes confuse your colleagues.

Build a firstOfflineName pipeline out of small functions: it returns the name of the first user whose status is offline, or the string "nobody" if there is no such user. Use isStatus and getName from the starter and the Sanctuary functions filter, head, map and fromMaybe, as in the lesson. Check the pipeline on both lists.
